## TL;DR

Review reports are now committed with the task branch at `work/reports/<task-id>/review-<pass>.md`, beside the engineering `round-<n>.json` files. A shared `report-paths` module is the single source of truth for both locations, readers still accept the pre-#1013 directories, and a one-time control-plane migration moves legacy engineering rounds onto `main`. Report commits advance the handoff snapshot and review lock, and the automatic review tree identity skips pure report commits, so a pass cannot invalidate itself or trigger a re-review. The Dev tab now reuses the Review tab's toolbar and pane classes, with Report on the left, Chat on the right, and the model/agent selector above the sub-tab selector.

## Work and rationale

The first decision was where the canonical history lives. `work/reports/<task-id>/` keeps both halves of the loop together without inventing a new top-level tree, so task bookkeeping stays inside `work/`. `src/core/report-paths.ts` centralizes the path helpers, the legacy engineering path, and `isOwnReportPath`. Every guard now asks that function instead of re-implementing prefix checks, which also closes the prefix-collision hazard where task `099` could match `0997`.

Writing a review pass is a three-part operation in `review-report-store.ts`: write the tracked file, commit only that path (`git commit --only`), then advance the handoff snapshot and review lock to the new HEAD. The snapshot refresh is deliberate rather than teaching every downstream consumer to ignore report commits; it keeps the invariant that the recorded sha is the tree the reviewer approved, while the commit is provably clean and limited to one file. `review-tree-identity.ts` still walks back over report-only commits so the automatic review decision compares code identity rather than the ever-moving branch tip. I also gave the unresolved-findings reader a committed-pass fallback: a fresh clone has no cache mirror, so without it a re-handoff after review feedback would silently lose the findings.

Bookkeeping classification was widened in one place per layer: `isForbiddenTaskScopePath` in landable, `isTaskBookkeepingPath` and the drift filter in `git.ts`, close-out's `resetForeignWorkFiles`, the review guard's staged-work filter, and handoff's report-commit recognition. All take an optional task id and exempt only that task's reports. Task markdown remains broadly bookkeeping, but `work/reports/` is explicitly carved out so another task's pass cannot ride along.

The migration calls the same move logic at boot on the control plane and commits the paths on `main`, never on a feature branch, because moving another task's files from a branch is exactly the cross-task drift the landable check rejects. A failed commit records its paths in the cache directory and retries on the next boot. The UI change replaces the bespoke `dev-report-toggle` with the Review tab's `review-toolbar`/`review-pane-tabs`/`review-pane` structure; Report comes first, and the agent selector sits above the toolbar so it stays visible on both panes.

## Approaches tried

I considered writing review reports only during close-out. That loses the report if a task stalls in review, never lands, or is abandoned, and it hides the current pass from the human while it matters most. I also considered telling close-out to ignore any commit whose paths are reports instead of advancing the snapshot. That weakens the drift guard and leaves every future bookkeeping type needing its own exception, so the snapshot refresh plus a narrow code-identity walk was the safer combination.

## Challenges and blockers

A pass can exist in both the tracked directory and the legacy cache during upgrade. Pass allocation now scans both and takes the maximum, so numbers are never reused; readers prefer the committed copy. Engineering rounds can also exist in both locations; the canonical file wins and a differing legacy copy is left untouched rather than silently dropped.

The test environment was under heavy load from another worktree, and the session's `TMPDIR` was deleted mid-run, which made `mkdtemp` fail in the contrast audit, UI smoke and one adoption-matrix case. Re-running with a fresh explicit `TMPDIR` passed: 6861 of 6863 local tests passed, and the one failure passed in isolation. No human-only verification is needed.

## Key learnings

"Bookkeeping" is task-scoped, not directory-scoped. Treating all of `work/*.md` as safe was fine until reports got a structured, per-task location; the id-aware predicate is the durable shape for future report kinds. Also, any write that moves HEAD after a review must either update the handoff recorded sha or make the identity comparison skip it — doing both is what keeps review, drift and re-review logic honest.
